evidence.quote: The first step in implementing OAuth2 is registering a developer application and retrieving your client ID and client secret.
Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app's settings.
Using an OAuth2 bearer token gained through the OAuth2 API.
All OAuth2 token endpoints require either HTTP Basic authentication or credentials supplied in the form data body
SaseQ/discord-mcp (493 stars) - community-maintained MCP server for Discord
Bot users are automatically added to all apps, and are authenticated using the bot token found in your app's settings.

result.notes: Discord's developer portal (discord.com/developers/applications) lets anyone register an application and generate a bot token / OAuth2 client credentials for free, no approval gate for standard bot/API scopes (privileged intents like message content require a form but not blocking basic API access). API is REST with a large surface (guilds, channels, users, webhooks, interactions, etc., several hundred endpoints) plus a Gateway websocket for real-time events. No official vendor-published MCP server found; several community MCP servers exist (SaseQ/discord-mcp, moltis, gortex, Smithery listings).
result.one_liner: Discord is a voice/text/community chat platform with a REST API and Gateway websocket for building bots and integrations.
